applies_why: The judge text relies on the almah/bethulah word-count cutting both ways as part of the reason to mark the point UNDERDETERMINED.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: Phrase: 'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.' Reading A: a two-sense word/verse cannot make the issue open or UNDERDETERMINED; both senses stand. Reading B: if lexical evidence cuts both ways, the issue may be open/UNDERDETERMINED. I adopt Reading A.
why: The judge marks the point UNDERDETERMINED partly because the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways, treating a two-sense matter as open contrary to K-S2's requirement that both senses stand.
